title: Self-sovereignty beyond money
tweets:
Bitcoin started as a monetary idea.

But the principle at its core — own your keys, verify everything, trust no one with what you can control yourself — doesn't stop at money.

It's a way of thinking that bleeds into everything else. 🧵

Self-custody means no third party between you and what's yours.

Apply that to money → Bitcoin in cold storage.
Apply that to time → you decide where it goes, not a job title.
Apply that to decisions → your values set the standard, not someone else's approval.

Most people rent their time.

They trade it for a salary, call it security, and quietly accept that someone else determines how 40 hours of every week gets spent.

That's a custodial arrangement. You have the balance. Someone else holds the keys.

Most people also outsource their beliefs.

They inherit opinions from their parents, their algorithm, their peer group. They mistake familiarity for conviction.

If you've never stress-tested what you believe, you don't own it. You're holding it on someone else's behalf.

The question Bitcoin taught me to ask — "who actually controls this?" — applies everywhere.

Who controls your time? Your income? Your opinion? Your identity?

Most people, when they trace it back, find someone other than themselves at the end of the chain.

Self-sovereignty isn't a Bitcoin feature.

It's a commitment to be the final authority on your own life — to hold the keys to everything that matters and accept the weight of that responsibility.

Bitcoin makes it possible financially. The rest is up to you.
